script: Hitler didn't invent the lie that killed six million people. He inherited it. In 1918 Germany lost the First World War, and the generals who lost it needed someone else to blame. Ludendorff and Hindenburg told the country the army was never defeated in the field — it was stabbed in the back at home. By socialists. By Jews. It wasn't true. The German army was collapsing and its own commanders knew it. But the lie was easier to live with than the loss. Hitler was a corporal in a hospital bed when he heard it, and he built a career on repeating it. Twenty-three years later, fifteen men met in a lakeside villa outside Berlin for ninety minutes. They ate lunch. They turned the lie into a schedule: trains, quotas, camps, eleven million names. That villa is still there. You can walk into the room, and the minutes are on the wall — thirty copies were made, twenty-nine were burned, and one survived. It's the reason we know exactly what was said. Because the lie that killed six million people wasn't invented by Hitler — he inherited it.

title: Two Generals Invented the Lie Hitler Used to Kill 6 Million
description:
Germany's own commanders knew the army was beaten in 1918. They told the country it had been stabbed in the back instead — and Hitler spent twenty years repeating a lie invented by the men who lost the war.

The Wannsee villa is still standing, and one of the thirty copies of the minutes survived the burning. That single page is why we know exactly what was said in those ninety minutes.

Who carries more of the blame: the men who invented the lie, or the man who used it?
